key_insight: A parameter-regularised ensemble Kalman filter can sequentially infer RANS turbulence-model parameters on a simple urban case and transfer them to more complex city geometries while staying within physically plausible ranges.
engineering_relevance: This improves the reliability of urban CFD for building ventilation, pollutant dispersion, and micrometeorology, while reducing the cost of manual turbulence-model tuning.
method: Infer RANS closure parameters sequentially with a Parameter-Regularised EnKF.
Use prior knowledge as regularisation to keep Bayesian updates physically bounded.
Train on an isolated building and transfer the inferred parameters to progressively harder urban cases.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the method reduces parameter uncertainty by about an order of magnitude and lowers reconstruction errors by up to 50% across benchmark transfer cases.
watch_item: Transferability is demonstrated on a limited set of urban scenarios, so performance may still depend on the chosen prior, sensor/data availability, and the degree of geometric or flow-regime mismatch.
paper_title: Transferable inference of turbulence models for urban flows with the Parameter-Regularised Ensemble Kalman Filter
